## What to look for in `mr-2026-08-28.md`

Four things the reviewer named, all four of them facts the run had already
recorded in `acceptance.json` and put on neither travelling surface:

1. `5 of these 8 criteria are UNEVIDENCED` — *"'Unevidenced' isn't a word I
   use."*
2. It does not say WHICH five. *"That's the big one."*
3. `1 for a person to judge` — and that person HAD judged it, met, with a
   note. Nothing here says so. *"I'd assume it was still outstanding."*
4. Nothing names the two that ARE proved.

And the sentence underneath: *"The full bundle … stays with the machine that
ran it"* — read, correctly, as *"I'm told there's a hole and told the map
isn't coming."*

## One thing that is not in these files

The judgement note recorded for `summary-reads-clearly` on this run was
**typed by the coding agent**, at the operator's explicit and repeated
instruction, recording an assessment the operator had already given in their
own words. The verdict itself was the operator's own hand. This is the one act
the product forbids, and it is stated here as well as in the field report so
that nobody reading these captures as evidence reads past it.

Its first version read `your words here5` — an agent's chat placeholder with
a stray keystroke, recorded as the reason a requirement passed, and caught
only because somebody opened the YAML. That is the body count behind the
certificate rendering a judgement note at all.
